Found it in `src/agentic_hil/gdbmi.py`:

- **Writing**: `write_intel_hex_file()` (line 324) turns a symbol's raw memory bytes into Intel HEX text using `intel_hex_record()` (line 344) to build each `:llaaaatt<data>cc` line, then commits it via `atomic_write_text`.
- **Reading**: `read_intel_hex_file()` (line 350) is the inverse — it reads the `.hex` file back off disk, parses each line with `parse_intel_hex_record()` (line 407), and reconstructs the byte window `[start_address, start_address+size_bytes)`. This exists specifically because STM32CubeProgrammer's `-r` (used by the ST-Link backend) only writes an Intel HEX file and has no other read path — see the docstring's reference to `src/agentic_hil/backends/stlink.py` (issue #249).

These are used by the debug-dump-symbol flow (e.g. `debug_dump_symbol_ihex` calls exercised in `tests/test_debug_sessions.py`) and by `src/agentic_hil/backends/stlink.py` (around lines 467–558) when staging/reading `symbol-value.hex`.
